theory.intro: $|X|$ is the distance of $X$ from $0$. For $k > 0$, $|X| < k$ means $X$ is within $k$ of $0$, one interval; $|X| > k$ means $X$ is further than $k$ away, two separate pieces.
facts: Write a union as $x < -a$ or $x > b$, never as the chained form $b < x < -a$, which no number satisfies.
Since $|X| \ge 0$, if $k < 0$ then $|ax + b| < k$ has no solution and $|ax + b| > k$ is true for all real $x$.
When $k = 0$: $|ax + b| \le 0$ only at $ax + b = 0$; $< 0$ never; $\ge 0$ always; $> 0$ for all $x$ except $x = -\dfrac{b}{a}$.
$|b - ax| = |ax - b|$, so reversing the order inside the bars gives the same solution.
steps: Check the sign of the constant right-hand side (if negative or zero, apply non-negativity properties directly).
Identify the inequality type: split $<, \le$ into a double inequality $-k < ax + b < k$, or $>, \ge$ into two separate inequalities $ax + b < -k \text{ or } ax + b > k$.
State the final solution set as a single interval, a union of intervals, a single point, or state all real $x$ / no solution.

development.solution_text:
Since $|4x + 7| \ge 0$ for all real $x$, an absolute value cannot be strictly less than $-5$.
No solution

Since $|6x - 1| \ge 0 \ge -3$ for all real $x$, the inequality holds for all real $x$.
All real $x$

$|5x - 8| \ge 0$ for all real $x$, and equals $0$ when $5x - 8 = 0 \implies x = \dfrac{8}{5}$.
All real $x$ except $x = \dfrac{8}{5}$

Restriction: $x \neq 3$.
Reciprocating positive terms gives:
$|x - 3| < \dfrac{1}{4}$
$-\dfrac{1}{4} < x - 3 < \dfrac{1}{4}$
$\dfrac{11}{4} < x < \dfrac{13}{4}$
Excluding $x = 3$:
$\dfrac{11}{4} < x < 3$ or $3 < x < \dfrac{13}{4}$

mastery.solution_text:
Restriction: $x \neq -\dfrac{1}{3}$.
Reciprocating gives:
$|3x + 1| \ge \dfrac{1}{2}$
$3x + 1 \le -\dfrac{1}{2}$ or $3x + 1 \ge \dfrac{1}{2}$
$3x \le -\dfrac{3}{2} \implies x \le -\dfrac{1}{2}$
$3x \ge -\dfrac{1}{2} \implies x \ge -\dfrac{1}{6}$
Since $x = -\dfrac{1}{3}$ lies between $-\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $-\dfrac{1}{6}$, no additional exclusion is needed.
$x \le -\dfrac{1}{2}$ or $x \ge -\dfrac{1}{6}$

Since $|4 - 5x| \ge 0$ for all real $x$, an absolute value cannot be strictly less than $0$.
No solution
